intro: You're looking for an EIS tax advisor near you, which suggests you're considering investing under the Enterprise Investment Scheme or already hold EIS shares and need help with the tax side. EIS reliefs are valuable but depend on meeting specific conditions, so getting the right advice matters. We can introduce you to a suitable UK tax adviser who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for an EIS tax advisor near me usually need
need_lead: Most people want clear, local guidance on how EIS reliefs work in their own circumstances.
needs: You are thinking about investing in an EIS-qualifying company and want to understand how income tax relief, capital gains deferral and loss relief would apply to you.
You already hold EIS shares and need help completing your tax return correctly, including how to claim relief and what records to keep.
You have EIS compliance certificates but are unsure how to use them or what happens if you lose them.
You are concerned about the holding period rules and want to know how they affect your relief if you sell or transfer shares.
You want to check that a company actually qualifies under EIS before you invest, or you run a company and need advice on compliance.
context_heading: One key thing to understand about EIS advice
context: "Tax adviser" is not a protected title in the UK, so anyone can call themselves one. The Chartered Institute of Taxation (CTA) and the Association of Taxation Technicians (ATT) are the main specialist bodies, and their members follow Professional Conduct in Relation to Taxation. Many accountants and solicitors also advise on tax.

Tax advisers who charge a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, and HMRC has been tightening standards for paid tax agents. It is sensible to ask about qualifications, supervision and professional indemnity insurance before you go ahead.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Whether you are considering a new EIS investment or already hold EIS shares and need help with your tax return.
The approximate amount you are thinking of investing, if that is relevant to your enquiry.
Whether you hold EIS compliance certificates and whether you need help understanding them.
Any specific concerns you have about holding periods, loss relief or capital gains deferral.
Whether you are an individual investor or advising a company on EIS compliance.
Your location and whether you prefer to meet in person, speak by phone or work remotely.
questions: What qualifications and professional body memberships do you hold?
How do you charge for EIS advice and what will the quote cover?
Can you explain how the holding period rules would affect my relief if my circumstances change?
What records should I keep to support my EIS claims, and for how long?
Are you supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes and do you have professional indemnity insurance?
How would you handle communication with HMRC if there is a query about my EIS relief?

faqs.q: Do I need a specialist EIS tax adviser or can my regular accountant help?
faqs.a: Many accountants can help with EIS reliefs, but if your affairs are complex or you are investing significant amounts, a specialist may be worthwhile. It is reasonable to ask about their experience with EIS before you proceed.

faqs.q: What information should I have ready before speaking to an EIS tax adviser?
faqs.a: Gather any EIS compliance certificates, details of the investment, and your previous tax returns. Also note any specific questions you have about reliefs or compliance.

faqs.q: Can iComply recommend a specific EIS tax adviser?
faqs.a: We introduce you to a suitable UK professional based on your needs, but we do not recommend or endorse any particular adviser. You should satisfy yourself that they are right for you.

faqs.q: How do I know if an EIS tax adviser is properly qualified?
faqs.a: Check whether they are a member of a recognised body such as the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians, and ask about their experience with EIS. Also confirm they have professional indemnity insurance.
